title: Increasing-cutoff stress for the Hamiltonian carre-du-champ comparison
question: Does the finite E_kin versus D_q comparison from R-402 remain two-sided when the oscillator cutoff is increased, or does the coordinate form become too small for a uniform upper comparison?
method: Use the volume-two actual Q3 chain and increase the one-site oscillator dimension through 12.
Retain beta in {1/2,1,2}, both source signs, both history signs, both split orders, every prefix, both history adjoints and both collar orientations while caching only exact finite prefixes.
Compute the physical-coordinate form D_q and the kinetic carré-du-champ E_kin on every declared conditional likelihood row, excluding only rows at or below the manifest ratio floor.
Record minimum and maximum ratios at each cutoff and compare the late profile with the d=3 baseline, keeping lower and upper directions separate.
Run a non-importing independent reconstruction, a momentum-mutation hostile lane and Lean scalar cross-check; integrate all artifacts with the release verifier.
finding: The primary lane passes 1397/1397 assertions over 7 systems, 2688 contexts and 21120 rows; the independent lane passes 1379/1379, the hostile lane 7/7, the integrated verifier 37/37 and Lean R403 compiles.  Of the rows, 15840 have nonzero D_q and their E_kin/D_q ratios range from 1.0461038216925114 to 109929.13074605557.  The per-cutoff maximum grows from 4.456994387884469 at d=3 to 109929.13074605557 at d=12, a factor 24664.408607934973.  The selected hostile context also grows from 4.44402... to 37605.8... while the p-to-q mutation is zero and the genuine late kinetic form is positive.
decision_reason: The finite ladder gives an explicit route-local stress against treating the R-402 interval as a cutoff-independent two-sided constant.  The lower ratio remains positive on the retained nonzero rows, so a possible one-sided lower-form route is not eliminated; however, finite growth is not a divergence theorem and does not establish an infinite-volume failure.  The honest verdict is inconclusive finite stress, with no new negative registry entry and no tier change.

adversarial_review.check: Minimum and maximum ratios are tracked separately at every cutoff; the growing maximum is not converted into a theorem about the infinite form.
Rows at or below the declared 1e-20 coordinate-form floor are counted separately and excluded from ratios; tolerances are manifest inputs.
The independent lane rebuilds the Q3 matrices, Gibbs states, prefixes and forms without importing the primary implementation and agrees within 5e-5.
Replacing p by the commuting coordinate q makes the mutated commutator zero while a genuine late kinetic row is positive.
Seven bounded oscillator dimensions show growth but no divergence or common-core limit is inferred.
No phase/volume/exhaustion uniformity, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure follows.

next_action: Prove or refute an analytic direction-specific E_kin versus D_q estimate on a cutoff-independent Hamiltonian common core, with constants uniform in source, phase, volume and exhaustion shape; repeat the phase and exhaustion stress before any R-399 shell-transfer promotion.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite increasing-cutoff stress only.  It proves no cutoff-independent or two-sided comparison, no divergence theorem, no common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The growing finite upper profile blocks automatic extrapolation of the R-402 interval but does not prove divergence of the infinite-volume ratio or disprove a separately proved one-sided estimate.
